newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline seen easing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline seen easing.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline prices were expected to come under pressure following a build in unleaded stocks in the Midwest refining region, traders said late Tuesday.

The American Petroleum Institute reported a 2.04 million barrel build in unleaded inventories and a modest 624,000 barrel build in distillate inventories, confirming earlier reports of increased shipments into the region.
The increased shipments preceeded a rash of turnarounds that have taken down units at several key Group Three refineries.
Midwest refineries were operating at 97.2 percent of capacity last week, down 2 percentage points following an outage that halved crude runs at Farmland Industries Inc.
Nationwide, refiners trimmed gasoline output to 52.8 percent of production yield from 54 percent, and boosted distillate output to 23.8 percent from 23.4 percent.
Group Three unleaded and diesel fuel differentials firmed early in the day on talk Texaco planned to begin a turnaround at its 94,600 barrel per day El Dorado, Kansas refinery this weekend.
Crude stocks in the Midwest PADD II region fell 1.5 million barrels on the week, which some traders read as a sign of planned autumn turnarounds.
